name: Merge Lifecycle Integration
description: Wire merge detection and execution into the existing lifecycle check loop in mesh/mesh.py, alongside fork and decay. Merge checks run at the same cadence as fork/decay. Pure detection functions compute signal overlap and assessment agreement between neighboring contexts; when thresholds are exceeded a MergeProposal is created. A planning phase collects all lifecycle proposals (fork, decay, merge), resolves conflicts, and executes them atomically within a single event-loop turn. In-flight signals routed to a merged context are re-routed to the surviving context via a redirect map with TTL-based cleanup. Decay-to-fork handoff is detected and converted to a merge-fold operation. All existing lifecycle tests must continue to pass.

functions.name: compute_signal_overlap
functions.description: Pure function. Computes the Jaccard-style signal ID overlap ratio between two sets of signal IDs. Returns |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|. Returns 0.0 if both sets are empty.

inputs.name: signals_a
inputs.description: Signal IDs from context A within the rolling window.

inputs.name: signals_b
inputs.description: Signal IDs from context B within the rolling window.

postconditions: Result is in [0.0, 1.0].
If both inputs are empty, result is 0.0.
Result is symmetric: compute_signal_overlap(a, b) == compute_signal_overlap(b, a).

functions.name: compute_assessment_agreement
functions.description: Pure function. Computes the agreement ratio between two sets of assessments on shared signals. Two assessments on the same signal 'agree' if they have the same decision AND their familiarity scores are within epsilon of each other. Returns count_of_agreements / count_of_shared_signals. Returns 0.0 if there are no shared signals.

error_cases.name: duplicate_signal_in_assessments
error_cases.condition: A single assessment list contains multiple assessments for the same signal_id.

error_data.detail: Assessment list contains duplicate signal_id entries.

postconditions: Result is in [0.0, 1.0].
If there are no shared signals between the two assessment lists, result is 0.0.
Result is symmetric: compute_assessment_agreement(a, b, eps) == compute_assessment_agreement(b, a, eps).

functions.name: check_merge
functions.description: Pure function. Evaluates whether two neighboring contexts should merge based on signal overlap and assessment agreement thresholds defined in config. Returns a MergeProposal if both thresholds are met, or None otherwise. Does not mutate any state.

error_data.detail: Cannot check merge of a context with itself.

preconditions: context_a and context_b are neighbors (context_b.context_id appears in context_a.neighbors or vice versa).
postconditions: If returned value is not None, then returned.overlap_score >= config.overlap_threshold and returned.agreement_score >= config.agreement_threshold.
If returned value is not None, source_context_id is the context with lower energy (tie-broken by lexicographic context_id), target_context_id is the other.
If returned value is None, at least one threshold was not met.

functions.name: execute_merge
functions.description: Pure function. Given two context snapshots and an approved MergeProposal, computes the MergeResult describing the merged state. Unions vector store signal sets (via signal_ids), deduplicates agent lists, takes max energy, computes topology patch (union of neighbors minus the two merging contexts, deduplicated). Does not apply any changes; returns a result to be applied by the caller.

inputs.name: context_a
inputs.description: Snapshot of the first context (must match one of the proposal's context IDs).

inputs.name: context_b
inputs.description: Snapshot of the second context (must match the other proposal context ID).

error_cases.name: context_id_mismatch
error_cases.condition: The context snapshot IDs do not match the proposal's source and target IDs.

error_data.detail: Context snapshot IDs do not match proposal source/target IDs.

error_cases.name: zero_energy_contexts
error_cases.condition: Both contexts have energy <= 0.0, which indicates they may both be decayed.

error_data.detail: Cannot merge two contexts with zero or negative energy.

postconditions: result.surviving_context_id == proposal.target_context_id.
result.removed_context_id == proposal.source_context_id.
result.merged_energy == max(context_a.energy, context_b.energy).
All agent IDs from both contexts appear in result.merged_agent_ids with no duplicates.
result.redirect.removed_context_id == result.removed_context_id and result.redirect.surviving_context_id == result.surviving_context_id.
result.redirect.ttl_seconds == config.redirect_ttl_seconds.
result.topology_patch.surviving_context_id == result.surviving_context_id.
Neither surviving_context_id nor removed_context_id appear in topology_patch.new_neighbors.

functions.name: detect_decay_fold_candidates
functions.description: Pure function. Scans a set of lifecycle proposals to detect decay-to-fork handoff scenarios: a context is DECAYING and a neighboring context is FORKING into its territory. Returns additional DECAY_FOLD merge proposals that should replace or supplement the original decay/fork proposals.

inputs.name: proposals
inputs.description: All lifecycle proposals collected in this cycle.

inputs.name: context_snapshots
inputs.description: Snapshots of all contexts in the mesh for neighbor lookups.

postconditions: All returned proposals have kind == DECAY_FOLD.
Each returned proposal has exactly 2 affected_context_ids.
Each returned proposal has a non-None merge_proposal with is_decay_fold == true.

functions.name: resolve_lifecycle_conflicts
functions.description: Pure function. Given a list of all lifecycle proposals (fork, decay, merge, decay_fold), resolves conflicts where multiple proposals affect the same context. Priority order: FORK > MERGE/DECAY_FOLD > DECAY. Within the same priority, earlier timestamps win. Returns a LifecyclePlan with accepted and rejected proposals.

inputs.name: proposals
inputs.description: All lifecycle proposals including decay_fold candidates.

postconditions: Every proposal in the input appears in exactly one of accepted_proposals or rejected_proposals.
No two accepted proposals share any affected_context_id.
len(accepted_proposals) + len(rejected_proposals) == len(proposals).
All rejected proposals have an entry in conflict_reasons.

functions.name: check_lifecycle_guard
functions.description: Checks whether a context can transition to a new lifecycle state. Returns true if the context is currently STABLE and the transition is allowed; false otherwise. This is the atomic guard that must be called within a single event-loop turn before setting the state.

error_cases.name: invalid_desired_state
error_cases.condition: desired_state is STABLE or MERGED, which are not valid transition targets.

error_data.detail: Cannot explicitly transition to STABLE or MERGED via guard check.

preconditions: desired_state is one of FORKING, DECAYING, MERGING.
postconditions: Returns true only if lifecycle_states[context_id] is STABLE or context_id is not in lifecycle_states.
Returns false if lifecycle_states[context_id] is FORKING, DECAYING, MERGING, or MERGED.

functions.name: transition_lifecycle_state
functions.description: Atomically transitions a context's lifecycle state in the state map. Must be called immediately after check_lifecycle_guard returns true, with no intervening await.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: The mutable lifecycle state map to update in place.

error_cases.name: concurrent_state_change
error_cases.condition: The context's state changed between the guard check and this transition call (should not happen if no await intervenes, but defensively checked).

error_data.detail: Lifecycle state changed concurrently; aborting transition.

preconditions: check_lifecycle_guard was called and returned true for this context_id and a compatible desired_state immediately prior, OR new_state is STABLE (revert) or MERGED (post-merge).
postconditions: lifecycle_states[context_id] == new_state after call.

functions.name: apply_merge_result
functions.description: Side-effectful function. Applies a MergeResult to the mesh: updates the surviving context's agents, energy, and vector store; removes the source context; updates neighbor topology for all affected contexts; adds the redirect entry to the redirect map. This is the integration point in mesh/mesh.py.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: The lifecycle state map to update (surviving -> STABLE, removed -> MERGED).

inputs.name: redirect_map
inputs.description: The redirect map to update with the new redirect entry.

error_cases.name: surviving_context_not_found
error_cases.condition: The surviving context does not exist in the mesh.

error_data.detail: Surviving context not found in mesh.

error_cases.name: removed_context_not_found
error_cases.condition: The removed context does not exist in the mesh.

error_data.detail: Removed context not found in mesh.

error_cases.name: unexpected_lifecycle_state
error_cases.condition: Either context is not in MERGING state when apply is called.

error_data.detail: Context not in MERGING state; cannot apply merge result.

error_cases.name: merge_apply_failed
error_cases.condition: An unexpected error occurs during application (e.g., vector store error). Both contexts are reverted to STABLE.

error_data.detail: Merge application failed; contexts reverted to STABLE.

postconditions: lifecycle_states[merge_result.surviving_context_id] == STABLE.
lifecycle_states[merge_result.removed_context_id] == MERGED.
redirect_map contains an entry for merge_result.removed_context_id.
The surviving context has the merged agents, energy, and updated neighbors.
The removed context is no longer active in the mesh.
side_effects: Mutates the surviving context's state (agents, energy, vector store, neighbors).
Removes the source context from the mesh.
Adds a redirect entry to redirect_map.
Updates neighbor lists of third-party contexts per topology_patch.

functions.name: resolve_signal_redirect
functions.description: Resolves a target context ID through the redirect map, following chains if necessary (a merged context may redirect to another merged context). Returns the final surviving context ID, or the original ID if no redirect exists. Enforces a maximum chain depth to prevent cycles.

inputs.name: max_depth
inputs.description: Maximum redirect chain depth to follow.

error_cases.name: redirect_chain_too_deep
error_cases.condition: The redirect chain exceeds max_depth, indicating a possible cycle or excessively long chain.

error_data.detail: Redirect chain exceeded max_depth; possible cycle detected.

postconditions: Returned context ID is not a key in redirect_map (i.e., it is not a merged/removed context), OR max_depth was reached.
If target_context_id is not in redirect_map, it is returned unchanged.

functions.name: cleanup_expired_redirects
functions.description: Removes expired redirect entries from the redirect map based on their TTL and the current time. Also removes the MERGED lifecycle state entry for cleaned-up contexts.

inputs.name: redirect_map
inputs.description: The redirect map to clean up.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: The lifecycle state map to clean up MERGED entries.

inputs.name: current_time
inputs.description: The current time for TTL comparison.

postconditions: All entries in redirect_map where (created_at + ttl_seconds) < current_time have been removed.
Corresponding MERGED entries in lifecycle_states have been removed.
Return value equals the number of entries removed.
side_effects: Mutates redirect_map by removing expired entries.
Mutates lifecycle_states by removing MERGED entries for cleaned-up contexts.

functions.name: run_lifecycle_cycle
functions.description: Top-level integration function called from mesh/mesh.py's lifecycle check loop. Orchestrates a complete lifecycle cycle: (1) snapshot all contexts, (2) collect fork/decay/merge proposals, (3) detect decay-fold candidates, (4) resolve conflicts, (5) execute all accepted proposals (applying state guards, transitions, and side effects), (6) clean up expired redirects. Returns a report of everything that happened. This replaces separate _check_forks/_check_decays/_check_merges with a unified planning-then-execution approach.

inputs.name: current_time
inputs.description: Current time for window computation and TTL cleanup.

error_cases.name: lifecycle_cycle_fatal
error_cases.condition: A catastrophic error prevents the cycle from completing (e.g., mesh state corruption). All in-progress transitions are best-effort reverted to STABLE.

error_data.detail: Fatal error during lifecycle cycle; best-effort revert performed.

postconditions: All accepted proposals have been executed or appear in report.errors with contexts reverted to STABLE.
report.plan.accepted_proposals and report.plan.rejected_proposals are disjoint and cover all collected proposals.
Expired redirects have been cleaned up.
No context is left in MERGING state after this function returns (either STABLE or MERGED).
side_effects: Mutates lifecycle_states for all affected contexts.
Mutates redirect_map (adds new redirects, removes expired ones).
Mutates mesh context state (agents, energy, vector stores, topology) for all executed proposals.
Removes contexts that were absorbed in merges.

functions.name: check_merges
functions.description: Scans all pairs of neighboring contexts and returns MergeProposals for pairs that exceed the overlap and agreement thresholds. This is the merge-specific proposal collection step within the lifecycle cycle. Skips contexts not in STABLE state.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: Current lifecycle states; only STABLE contexts are considered.

postconditions: All returned proposals have overlap_score >= config.overlap_threshold and agreement_score >= config.agreement_threshold.
No proposal involves a context whose lifecycle_state is not STABLE.
Each unordered pair of contexts appears at most once in the result.

invariants: A context may be in at most one LifecycleState transition at any time; concurrent FORKING, DECAYING, and MERGING on the same context are mutually exclusive.
The lifecycle_states dict is the single source of truth for context lifecycle state; check-then-transition must occur within a single event-loop turn with no await between check and set.
After a merge completes, exactly one of the two input contexts survives; the other is removed and an entry is added to the redirect map.
Redirect map entries have a finite TTL and are cleaned up after expiry; no unbounded growth.
All pure functions (compute_signal_overlap, compute_assessment_agreement, check_merge, execute_merge, resolve_lifecycle_conflicts) are deterministic and produce no side effects.
Fork, decay, and merge proposals collected in the same cycle are conflict-resolved before any execution begins.
Existing fork and decay lifecycle behavior is unchanged; all pre-existing lifecycle tests must pass.
MergeConfig thresholds overlap_threshold and agreement_threshold default to 0.7 and 0.8 respectively but are configurable.
